clemson.citation: Mattfeld R., Jesch E., Hoover A. A new dataset for evaluating pedometer performance. IEEE BIBM 2017, doi:10.1109/BIBM.2017.8217769
clemson.licence: per upstream Pedometer Evaluation Project terms (cecas.clemson.edu/~ahoover/pedometer); not redistributed here
clemson.source: prepared copy github.com/ChaddBrenner/mattfeld_research_data (timelines aligned, channels min-max normalised over all participants)
clemson.labels: annotated left/right foot contacts ('l','r'); 'ledge'/'redge' kept separately
clemson.preprocessing_here: per-channel affine re-calibration to g (autocalibrate on the least-variable 1 s windows pooled over all 90 files); gyroscope unused (scale unrecoverable)

karas.citation: Karas M. et al. (2021) Labeled raw accelerometry data captured during walking, stair climbing and driving. PhysioNet, doi:10.13026/51h0-a262
karas.licence: Open Data Commons Open Database License v1.0
karas.placement: left wrist (ActiGraph GT3X+), 100 Hz; ankles used only for the derived step reference
karas.labels: activity per sample: 1 walking, 2 stairs down, 3 stairs up, 4 driving, 77 clapping, 99 non-study. No step annotations: walking steps are a DERIVED reference from the ankle sensors (see benchmarks/steps_bench.py), not a manual count
